entries.example: Friction opposes relative motion: a 60-newton push drives the block right, a 40-newton friction arrow grows at the contact against the slide, and the net 20 newtons to the right keeps the block sliding.
entries.meaning: The force between two surfaces in contact that opposes their relative slide - which is why it can point forward on a driving wheel.

entries.example: Friction opposes relative motion: a 60-newton push drives the block right, a 40-newton friction arrow grows at the contact against the slide, and the net 20 newtons to the right keeps the block sliding.
entries.meaning: The single force left after opposing forces are combined: a 60 N push against 40 N of friction leaves a net 20 N.

entries.example: Moments: 60 newtons at 0.5 metres makes 30 newton-metres on the left; 30 newtons at 0.75 metres makes only 22.5 on the right, so the beam tips - then the right weight slides to 1.0 metre, its moment rises to 30, and the beam balances.
entries.meaning: The turning effect of a force, calculated as force times distance from the pivot, measured in newton-metres.

entries.example: Moments: 60 newtons at 0.5 metres makes 30 newton-metres on the left; 30 newtons at 0.75 metres makes only 22.5 on the right, so the beam tips - then the right weight slides to 1.0 metre, its moment rises to 30, and the beam balances.
entries.meaning: The fixed point a beam or lever turns around; every moment distance is measured from it.

entries.example: A 200 N crate rests on its wide face of area 0.5 square metres. Pressure = force / area = 200 / 0.5 = 400 Pa. Check the units: newtons divided by square metres gives pascals, and tipping the crate onto a smaller face raises the pressure without changing the force.
entries.meaning: Force spread over an area, calculated as force divided by area, measured in pascals.

entries.example: Pressure: a 200-newton crate on a 0.5-square-metre face gives 400 pascals; tipped onto a 0.05-square-metre edge the same force gives 4000 pascals - one tenth the area, ten times the pressure.
entries.meaning: The unit of pressure: one pascal is one newton spread over one square metre.
